title: One-argument oracle-call step
statement: Let $\ell$ be a label, $j\in\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, $r\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of the four registers. If the instruction at $\ell$ calls oracle $j$ in unary-first mode with the single register $r$, with successor labels $\ell_1$ and $\ell_0$ for positive and negative answers, respectively, then one machine step from the configuration with label $\ell$, registers $v$, and no answer leaves the registers unchanged and no answer recorded, and moves to $\ell_1$ exactly when the oracle accepts the encoding of the unary string $1^n$ paired with the binary representation of $v(r)$; otherwise it moves to $\ell_0$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $\ell$ is the specified one-register oracle call
